The bug was in the code, not the test. I opened the fix as PR #2409: https://github.com/openagt/openagent/pull/2409

**The race:** When Ctrl+K opens the jump, its field is drawn right away, but Base UI only moves the focus into it on the next frame, about 14 ms later. The test types as soon as the field appears. In the failing runs, the `j` arrived at about 12 ms, so it went to the launcher's message box behind the jump. That box then had text, so its "Start agent" button slid in under the jump. That slide is the layout shift the test catches, which is why the shifted element in the error had no name. The launcher also kept the stray "j" as its draft. A person typing fast, or on a busy page, could lose their first letter the same way.

**The fix:**
- `packages/ui/dashboard/components/JumpPalette.tsx`: the field gets `autoFocus`, so it has the caret as soon as it is drawn and no keystroke can get in between.
- `JumpPalette.test.tsx`: the test for opening the jump now checks the focus as soon as the field exists instead of waiting first. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

**Runs:**
- **Before the fix:** 3 of 12 runs of the smoke-test file failed on this shift. A test-name pattern didn't narrow the run, so all 6 smoke tests in the file ran each time.
- **After the fix:** 20 runs, none failed on the shift. Three still failed: two timed out in this test waiting for the run to ask "Which way?" right after Start, before the jump is used, and one timed out in the question-answering test. All three happened while the machine's load average was about 13 because of the other sessions.
- **Checks before pushing:** `pnpm typecheck` passes, and so do the tests of `@openagt/ui`, `@openagt/install` and `@openagt/dashboard` (the package I changed and the two that depend on it), run once.
